decisions.reason: Its proven government use and strong fit with aviation and border-security operations make it a strategic core product with very low withdrawal risk.

As travel-health compliance has likely become less central by 2025, this product looks more vulnerable to declining demand and portfolio rationalisation despite some adjacency to our passenger-processing offer.
Cyber security awareness training matches our training capabilities, cross-sells well to existing clients, and benefits from persistent security demand across critical infrastructure.
Behaviour analysis remains aligned with our integrated security positioning, though adoption, privacy scrutiny, and longer enterprise sales cycles still create moderate risk.
Passenger security profiling carries the highest regulatory, reputational, and customer-acceptance risk in Germany and shows the weakest visible traction, so it is the clearest candidate to exit.
Travel and document verification is close to our established offer, relevant for transport and border-related customers, and appears to have durable practical value in operations.
